title: Propublica reported that a firm tied to DHS Chief Kristi Noem was
description_short: Propublica reported that a firm tied to DHS Chief Kristi Noem was paid $200 million in DHS ad contracts during the government shutdown
description_medium: ProPublica reported that DHS’s more than $200 million immigration-ad campaign used a newly created Delaware company as the public contractor while a politically connected South Dakota firm, the Strategy Group, did campaign work. The report linked the firm to Kristi Noem and her senior aides. It does not establish that the Strategy Group received the full $200 million.
description_long: During the 2025 government shutdown, Homeland Security Secretary Kristi Noem traveled to Mount Rushmore to film an immigration advertisement as part of a taxpayer-funded campaign worth more than $200 million. ProPublica reported that DHS invoked a border emergency to award the campaign contracts without normal competitive bidding. Public contract records named a Delaware company formed days before the deal was finalized, leaving at least one beneficiary undisclosed. The company producing the Mount Rushmore shoot was the Strategy Group, a Republican consulting firm with long-standing ties to Noem’s political operation. The firm worked on her 2022 gubernatorial campaign; Noem aide Corey Lewandowski had worked extensively with it, and its chief executive was married to DHS spokesperson Tricia McLaughlin. Contracting experts said the relationships raised serious ethics questions. ProPublica described the Strategy Group’s work as the first known instance of campaign money flowing from Noem’s agency to businesses controlled by her allies. The reporting supports scrutiny of the contracting process and undisclosed beneficiaries, but the supplied article does not say the Strategy Group itself received all $200 million. That distinction matters to the headline’s claim about the amount paid to the firm.

title: U.S. Citizen Dulce Diaz Morales Held 25 Days After ICE Rejected Her Maryland Birth Certificate
description_short: U.S. Citizen Dulce Diaz Morales Held 25 Days After ICE Rejected Her Maryland Birth Certificate
description_medium: In late 2025, 22-year-old Dulce Consuelo Diaz Morales was arrested by ICE agents despite her attorneys providing her Maryland birth certificate proving she was born in the United States. DHS contested her citizenship claim, alleging she entered the country illegally, and held her in an immigrant detention facility for 25 days before finally releasing her. Her case was cited by ProPublica in April 2026 alongside the Brian Morales deportation as evidence that ICE agents are systematically ignoring documentary proof of citizenship.
description_long: In late 2025, ICE detained Dulce Consuelo Diaz Morales, a 22-year-old Maryland woman whose attorneys said they provided the agency with her state birth certificate as proof that she was born in the United States. DHS disputed her citizenship claim and alleged that she had entered the country illegally. Diaz Morales remained in immigration detention for 25 days before being released. The dispute centered on how officials treated a document that, according to her attorneys, established her U.S. birth. The case was later cited by ProPublica alongside the deportation of Brian Morales in its reporting on immigration officers’ handling of citizenship evidence. That broader reporting raised questions about how citizenship claims were evaluated, but Diaz Morales’s detention and release do not by themselves establish a system-wide practice or reveal why officials initially rejected the certificate. The available account describes the competing claims and the duration of detention; it does not provide the agency’s full records, the legal basis for its initial decision or a court finding about the case. Her release ended the 25-day detention, while the reasons for the disputed citizenship determination remain a central part of the documented episode.

title: SpaceX Positioned as Frontrunner for 'Golden Dome' Missile Defense
description_short: SpaceX Positioned as Frontrunner for 'Golden Dome' Missile Defense
description_medium: A group of 42 Democratic lawmakers led by Sen. Elizabeth Warren requested a Defense Department Inspector General probe in May 2025 into Elon Musk's role in the bidding process for the 'Golden Dome' missile defense system. Reuters reported SpaceX, along with Palantir and Anduril, had emerged as frontrunners for the project while Musk was simultaneously serving as a senior White House adviser overseeing agencies that would oversee SpaceX contracts.
description_long: In May 2025, 42 Democratic lawmakers led by Senator Elizabeth Warren asked the Defense Department inspector general to examine Elon Musk’s role in the Golden Dome missile-defense procurement. Reuters had reported that SpaceX, Palantir and Anduril were emerging as front-runners to build key parts of the system. SpaceX was working with the two technology companies on a proposal involving hundreds of satellites to detect and track missiles; the project’s structure and contractor selection were still at an early stage. Musk had donated heavily to Trump’s campaign and was serving as a White House adviser on government spending. The Guardian reported that the SpaceX group met with administration and Pentagon officials, while sources described the process as unusually deferential to Musk. SpaceX and Musk declined to comment on his involvement in contract discussions, and the Pentagon said it would provide options for the president to decide. Being a leading bidder did not mean SpaceX had received an award, and the reporting did not establish that Musk intervened in the bid process. The lawmakers’ request sought oversight of a potential conflict, not confirmation that favoritism occurred.
